original_question: If A is a set of positive integers such that the reciprocal series sum_{n in A} 1/n diverges, must A contain arithmetic progressions of arbitrarily large finite length?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Conjecture 1 (P. Erdös), introduced right after Problem 3 and immediately before Theorem 7: if the reciprocal sum over a set diverges, then the set contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core statement of the paper's Conjecture 1 almost exactly: the hypothesis is divergence of the reciprocal subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n, and the conclusion is the existence of arithmetic progressions of unbounded finite length inside A. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
missing_details: Make the ambient set explicit: the surrounding discussion in Section 5 is about subseries of the harmonic series, and Problem 3 is stated for A subset of N, so the stand-alone version should say A subset of N = {1,2,3,...}. Conjecture 1 itself says 'a set A of integers', but the local context is clearly the positive-integer/harmonic-series setting. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
Clarify that divergence means ordinary divergence of the positive series sum_{n in A} 1/n. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))

Unpack 'arbitrarily long' into an explicit quantifier: for every integer k >= 3, there should exist a k-term arithmetic progression contained in A. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
Define the progression explicitly in the stand-alone version: a, a+r, ..., a+(k-1)r with integers a >= 1 and r >= 1. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))

Keep the statement about exact arithmetic progressions, not approximate ones; epsilon-progressions appear only in Theorem 7 as a consequence assuming the conjecture, not as the conjecture itself. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))

Do not add extra hypotheses such as positive upper density, and do not strengthen the conclusion to many progressions or large common differences; those are discussed separately from the formal conjecture. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
refined_question: Let A be a subset of N = {1,2,3,...}. If the positive subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n diverges, must it follow that for every integer k >= 3 there exist integers a >= 1 and r >= 1 such that a, a+r, ..., a+(k-1)r all belong to A?
justification: The draft is already a near-verbatim paraphrase of the paper's Conjecture 1, not of the neighboring weighted-density Problem 3 and not of Theorem 7's epsilon-progression consequence. The only real sharpening needed is to make the domain N explicit from the Section 5 harmonic-series context and to spell out the progression quantifier so the question is fully stand-alone. ([aos.ro](https://www.aos.ro/wp-content/anale/MVol6Nr1Art.5.pdf))
